pages.title: The Engagement
pages.content:
The Engagement

Five stages from the first enquiry to the crew in the room three hours before your guests.

Start an enquiry

Reply within 1 working day

Tasting about 3 weeks before

Crew 3 hours before guests

Start an enquiry

Five stages

— FROM THE FIRST TASTING TO THE NIGHT OF SERVICE —

STEP 01

Enquiry

Day 0

Name the date, place, and guests. We reply within one working day.

STEP 02

Tasting

About 3 weeks before

Taste the menu with us and agree what the table should serve.

STEP 03

Menu & floor plan

2 weeks before

We draw the table plan and lock the menu for your room.

STEP 04

Final numbers

5 days before

Confirm the guest count so the kitchen and crew match your booking.

STEP 05

Night of service

3 hours before

The crew arrives, sets the room, and serves until the evening ends.

From the first tasting to the night of service

An Enishi engagement is five stages, counted from the day you write to us. We reply within one working day. A tasting for two is $60 and is credited on the booking. The menu and floor plan are settled about two weeks before the date. Final guest numbers are due five days before. On the day, the crew is in the room three hours before your guests.

Events may run any day until 23:30. We cook for 12 to 180 guests, from the kitchen at 14 Wharf Lane, Harbourside, and we travel within 40 kilometres. A 30 percent deposit holds the date. Service staff are $38 per staff hour. Office hours for planning are Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 18:00. Tastings are Thursdays and Fridays, 14:00 to 17:00.

ENQUIRY DAY 0

Enquiry

Stage 01 is the enquiry, on day 0. You tell us the date, the place, the occasion and a first guess at numbers, anywhere from 12 to 180. We answer within one working day, in office hours Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 18:00. In that reply we say whether the date is open, which of the menus can fit the room, and how the 30 percent deposit confirms the hold.

You do not need a finished guest list. You do need a room that is already yours: an office, a hired hall, or a family table. We do not sell alcohol. If you want it poured, it is yours, and the service lead plans how it is served beside the food. Nothing is cooked until the later stages.

Reply in 1 working day

12–180 guests

Reply1 working day

TASTING 3 WEEKS BEFORE

Tasting

Stage 02 is the tasting, about three weeks before the event. Two of you sit with the kitchen over six small plates and a notebook. The tasting is $60 for two, and that $60 is credited on the booking. Slots are Thursdays and Fridays, 14:00 to 17:00, at 14 Wharf Lane. You say what should stay, what should be quieter, and who at the table needs a different plate.

We write the changes into the menu that will be costed for the whole party. This is the moment the food stops being a price list and becomes the meal you will actually be served. If the date is an office lunch rather than an evening, the same kitchen still cooks it, with 48 hours' notice and a minimum of 12.

Thu & Fri 14:00–17:00

FLOOR PLAN 2 WEEKS BEFORE

Menu and floor plan

Stage 03 is the menu and floor plan, two weeks before. You confirm the menu and tell us how the room is already furnished. We draw the table plan by hand and match it to the way the crew will set linen and glass. A seated banquet is three courses at $72 a guest, minimum 30. A family celebration buffet is $46 a guest, minimum 20.

A canapé reception is eight pieces at $34 a guest, minimum 20. The plan shows where plates land, where a cake stand sits, and where staff move. You approve it before we buy. Service staff remain $38 per staff hour, counted for the hours the crew is with you, including the three hours in the room before guests arrive.

NUMBERS 5 DAYS BEFORE

Final numbers

Stage 04 is final numbers, five days before. You send the guest count we will cook and staff for. That count replaces the estimate from the enquiry. We buy, prep and schedule against it, within the minimum for the menu you chose: 12 for a working breakfast or an office lunch box, 20 for a buffet or a canapé reception, 30 for a seated banquet.

Dietary notes travel with this list, not as a surprise on the night. If someone drops out after this point, the kitchen has already committed to the figure you sent. The 30 percent deposit has already confirmed the date. The balance follows the final count and the staff hours at $38.

Dietary notes travel with the count

SERVICE 3 HOURS BEFORE

Night of service

Stage 05 is the night of service. The crew arrives three hours before your guests, loads out of a plain van, and sets the room so the table is finished before anyone walks in. Service can run until 23:30. Rafael Costa leads the floor. Mireille Duval's kitchen, with Tomasz Wren and Ayo Okafor, has already plated or trayed the menu you tasted.

Lena Hartmann has the floor plan. For an office lunch, Priya Raman has scheduled delivery inside the 48-hour window. We clear what we brought. You keep the room, the drinks you supplied, and the evening. The same five stages apply whether the table is a birthday, a glasshouse engagement dinner, or a banquet in a hired hall.

pages.title: Office Catering
pages.content:
Office Catering

Cooked at 14 Wharf Lane and laid on your meeting table. 48 hours’ notice, minimum 12.

Order a lunch

Notice 48 hours

Minimum 12 guests

Delivery within 40 km

Start an enquiry

Lunches that land at the meeting table

Office catering from Enishi is cooked at 14 Wharf Lane and delivered within 40 kilometres. Notice is 48 hours. The minimum is 12 guests. Breakfast and lunch boxes are priced per guest. An afternoon canapé reception uses the same kitchen and needs a minimum of 20. Orders are taken Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 18:00, by phone on +1 555 0142 or by email at hello@enishi-catering.example.

Priya Raman coordinates office work: she confirms the headcount, the delivery time and the dietary notes, then the kitchen preps. We do not sell alcohol. If a meeting is marking something, the client's own drinks can be poured by service staff at $38 per staff hour. A larger celebration still belongs on the three-week engagement path.

BREAKFAST FOR THE MORNING

Breakfast

The working breakfast table is $14 a guest, minimum 12. It is laid on your meeting table: bread, grain salads and the savoury plates the kitchen has set for that morning, meant to be eaten while the first session starts. You send the count and the time at least 48 hours ahead. We deliver within 40 kilometres of Harbourside.

Tell Priya where the table is, whether there is a kitchen or only a boardroom, and what should be kept aside for dietary needs. There is no separate venue fee from us. The room is yours. Staff, if you want someone to stay and clear, are $38 an hour. Most breakfasts are dropped, set, and left with your office coordinator.

Min 12

48 h notice

Working breakfast table$14

See the menus

LUNCH BOX FOR THE MEETING

Lunch box

The office lunch box set is $18 a guest, minimum 12. Boxes, grain salads and bread are packed for a working lunch and laid out on a pale table the way a meeting actually runs: people take a box and go back to the work. Notice is 48 hours. Final counts should be as accurate as you can make them when you order; the five-day rule is for evening events, while office lunches move on the 48-hour clock.

Dietary plates are marked when you have told us the need with the order. Delivery sits inside the 40-kilometre area. If the lunch is an all-hands for more than a small team, the same box can sit beside a small buffet, as it did for an architecture studio of 140.

Min 12

Individual boxes

Office lunch box set$18

See the menus

AFTERNOON FOR THE FAREWELL

Afternoon

The afternoon row is a canapé reception: eight pieces at $34 a guest, minimum 20. It suits a late meeting, a farewell in the studio, or a client afternoon where a full banquet would be too much and a lunch box too little. The pieces leave the kitchen on trays. A server can stay; service staff are $38 per staff hour.

If you would rather have the trays set and the meeting left private, say so when you order and we will plan the drop only. Alcohol is not on our price list. We will serve what you have bought, if that is part of the brief. Book at least 48 hours ahead, and earlier in a busy week, through the office coordinator.

Min 20

8 pieces each

See the menus

Order, delivery, collection

We take back our crates and trays and leave the room as found.

Office work runs in three steps. You order, with 48 hours' notice, a minimum of 12 for breakfast or lunch boxes, and a minimum of 20 if the afternoon is canapés. We confirm by the next working reply during Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 18:00. On the day we deliver to the address you gave, inside 40 kilometres of 14 Wharf Lane, and lay the food on the table you named.

Collection closes the job: we take back our crates and trays. Your room stays as we found the furniture. If the headcount changes, write to Priya Raman before the kitchen is in prep. A tasting is not required for a standard office order. It remains available on Thursday or Friday, 14:00 to 17:00, at $60 for two, credited if the order becomes a booked event.

pages.title: Celebrations
pages.content:
Celebrations

Birthdays, engagements and family tables, cooked as one meal and set before anyone arrives.

Plan a celebration

Buffet $46 per guest

Minimum 20 guests

Deposit 30 %

Start an enquiry

Birthdays, engagements and family tables

Family celebrations are cooked as one table, then carried to a room you have already hired or a home that can hold the party. The usual menu is the family celebration buffet at $46 a guest, minimum 20. We also cook a seated three-course banquet at $72, minimum 30, and a canapé reception of eight pieces at $34, minimum 20, when the gathering is standing rather than sitting.

Guest counts run from 12 to 180 across the company; for these menus the minimum on the price is the floor. Lead time is three weeks. The crew arrives three hours before the guests. Service ends by 23:30. A 30 percent deposit holds the date. Final numbers are due five days before.

BIRTHDAYS THE LONG TABLE

Birthdays

A birthday at Enishi is often a buffet in a hall that already means something to the family. The rowing-club lunch we cooked for a 60th birthday sat 84 guests at a buffet, with oars on the timber wall and the cake stand on the same table as the platters. The menu price was the family celebration buffet, $46 a guest. You choose the room. We bring the food, the linen setting and the crew.

Tell us about the cake: if it is yours, we leave a clear place for it and cut or serve as you ask. Staff are $38 an hour. We do not sell alcohol; if there is a toast, the bottles are yours and we serve them. Start three weeks out, taste on a Thursday or Friday if you want the menu adjusted, and send final numbers five days before.

ENGAGEMENTS ONE TABLE, THREE COURSES

Engagements

An engagement dinner wants one long table and a menu that was tasted, not guessed. We seated 36 guests for an engagement dinner inside a rented glasshouse: one table, three courses, the room already full of afternoon light before anyone arrived. A seated banquet is $72 a guest, minimum 30, so a party of 36 sits comfortably inside the card. The tasting for two is $60, credited on the booking, about three weeks before, on Thursday or Friday between 14:00 and 17:00.

Two weeks before, we draw the floor plan around the glass, the doors and the single table. The crew is in three hours early so the glasses are already in place when the couple arrives. Service may run until 23:30. The deposit is 30 percent.

FAMILY GATHERINGS

Family gatherings

A family gathering can be the buffet at $46, minimum 20, when several generations are passing bowls and leaving the table between courses. It can be canapés at $34, minimum 20, when the party starts on its feet. Children and elders belong in the dietary notes you send with the final count, five days before. The kitchen will cook the same menu with plates set aside, rather than a separate children's price; we do not keep a second rate.

Numbers still have to fall between the menu minimum and our ceiling of 180. The room might be a hired hall within 40 kilometres of Harbourside or a long table at home. You book the space. We book the cooking, the staff hours at $38, and the timing.

pages.title: Banquets & Halls
pages.content:
Banquets & Halls

Long-table work in a hall you hire: a set menu and a crew that has the room ready before the door opens.

Book a tasting

Guests 30 to 180 seated

Crew $38 per staff hour

Halls partner rooms within 40 km

Start an enquiry

Seated, buffet or canapé in a hall you hire

Banquets are the long-table work: a hired hall, a set menu, and a crew that has the room ready before the door opens. We cook for parties inside our range of 12 to 180 guests, subject to each menu's minimum, and we travel within 40 kilometres of 14 Wharf Lane, Harbourside. You hold the contract with the hall. We hold the cooking, the floor plan and the service.

Lead time is three weeks. The deposit is 30 percent. Final numbers arrive five days before. The crew is in three hours before service, and the evening ends by 23:30. Staffing is $38 per staff hour. We do not sell alcohol. We serve the client's. Lena Hartmann plans the room; Rafael Costa leads service on the night.

SEATED THREE COURSES

Seated

A seated banquet is three courses at $72 a guest, minimum 30. Places are set, plates are carried, and the table is already linen and glass when guests come in. The glasshouse engagement for 36 was this menu: one long table, three courses, a rented room that was not ours. Two weeks before the date we draw the floor plan so service knows which side to approach and where a speech will stand.

The tasting, $60 for two and credited on the booking, is the right place to decide the three courses. On the night the crew's first three hours are setting, not cooking in a corridor. Hours of staffing at $38 cover that set-up as well as service through to 23:30. Dietary plates are fixed from the list you send five days before.

Min 30

Three courses

Seated banquet$72

Service staff$38 per hour

See the menus

BUFFET SHARED PLATTERS

Buffet

The buffet is $46 a guest, minimum 20. Platters are laid so guests serve themselves from a dressed table, with staff present to keep the line clear and the dishes replenished. The 60th birthday in the rowing-club hall used this menu for 84 guests. It is the same family celebration buffet, brought into a larger room and staffed for the length of the party.

Tell us whether the hall expects a single long board or a table guests walk around. We plan the platters to that shape at the menu stage, two weeks out. Cake, if it is yours, gets a gap on the linen. We still arrive three hours before the first guest. The room's own rules on closing time apply alongside our limit of 23:30.

CANAPÉ EIGHT PIECES

Canapé

A canapé reception is eight pieces at $34 a guest, minimum 20. Trays move through a standing party; a slate of small pieces is the opening picture, then the crew keeps them coming. This is the right row when the hall has no single seated plan, or when dinner is short and the evening is mostly conversation. Eight pieces is the stated menu, not a guess that grows on the night.

If you need more service than a drop, staff are $38 an hour and are scheduled with the three-hour arrival. Drinks remain yours. We will pour them and we will not invoice them, because we do not sell alcohol. Give us the hall's load-in rules when you enquire so the van time fits the building, not only our kitchen clock.

pages.title: Menus & Prices
pages.content:
Menus & Prices

Seven prices, published in US dollars, with the minimum beside each. The same figures appear everywhere on this site.

OFFICE ORDERED 48 HOURS AHEAD

Office menus need 48 hours' notice and a minimum of 12 guests. Prices are in US dollars per guest. The working breakfast table is $14. The office lunch box set is $18. Both are cooked at 14 Wharf Lane and delivered within 40 kilometres. The breakfast is laid on your meeting table. The lunch box set is individual boxes with grain salads and bread, set out for people who will eat and return to work.

Dietary plates can be separated when you name the need with the order. Service staff, if you want a person to stay, are listed under Banquets and extras at $38 per staff hour. A canapé afternoon for the office is also possible; it is priced with the reception menu, minimum 20, not as a third office box. Orders are confirmed in office hours, Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 18:00.

Working breakfast tablePer guest · minimum 12$14

Office lunch box setPer guest · minimum 12$18

CELEBRATIONS BIRTHDAYS AND FAMILY TABLES

The family celebration buffet is $46 a guest, minimum 20. It is the menu for birthdays, family gatherings and any long table where platters are shared. Lead time is three weeks, the deposit is 30 percent, and final numbers are due five days before. The crew arrives three hours before guests. A 60th birthday we served in a rowing-club hall used this buffet for 84 guests.

If the celebration should be seated, use the three-course banquet at $72, minimum 30, in the next group. If it should be standing, use the canapé reception at $34, minimum 20. Those two prices are not celebration surcharges. They are the same cards, chosen because of how the room will be used. Tastings for celebration menus are Thursdays and Fridays, 14:00 to 17:00.

Family celebration buffetPer guest · minimum 20$46

BANQUETS AND EXTRAS

A seated banquet, three courses, is $72 a guest, minimum 30. A canapé reception, eight pieces, is $34 a guest, minimum 20. A tasting for two is $60 per tasting and is credited on the booking. Service staff are $38 per staff hour. The tasting takes place at the kitchen about three weeks before an event. Staff hours include the crew's arrival three hours before guests and the service that follows, ending no later than 23:30.

The 30 percent deposit confirms the date. The balance is calculated from the final guest count, sent five days before, and from the staff hours you have agreed. We do not sell alcohol. If we serve drinks, they are the client's, and the staff time is the only charge. All of these figures are the same on every page of this site.

Canapé reception, 8 piecesPer guest · minimum 20$34

Seated banquet, three coursesPer guest · minimum 30$72

Tasting for twoPer tasting · credited on booking$60

Service staffPer staff hour$38

Dietary notes

Tell us about dietary needs twice: once at enquiry or tasting, and again with the final numbers five days before the event, or with the 48-hour office order. The kitchen cooks the agreed menu and sets aside the plates that have to differ. We do not keep a separate price for those plates. We need the note in time to buy and prep, which is why the five-day lock exists for events.

There is no list of diets we refuse and no list we claim to cover without hearing the detail. Write what the guest needs, plainly, to hello@enishi-catering.example or by phone on +1 555 0142. For an office lunch, Priya Raman marks the boxes. For an evening, Lena Hartmann carries the note onto the floor plan so service does not rely on memory.

A seasonal menu, in words

— THREE COURSES, THREE SEASONS —

The sample below is a picture of how three courses move through the year. It is not a second price list. Seated service remains $72 a guest. In the cooler months the first course is a grain salad with roasted roots and a sharp dressing; the main is a braise with a warm vegetable platter; the last course is a baked fruit with a spoon of cream from Ayo Okafor's pastry bench. In the mild months the first course is a green salad and a small tart; the main is a roast with herbs and a bowl of leaves; the last is a light cake cut for the table.

In the warm months the first course is tomatoes and bread; the main is a cold platter of vegetables and a simply cooked protein; the last is stone fruit. Buffet and canapé parties draw from the same seasons. The tasting is where your version of this list is decided.

A tasting for two is $60 and is credited on the booking.

pages.title: About
pages.content:
About

Enishi means the ties made at a shared table. Mireille Duval founded the company in 2014.

The ties made at a shared table

Enishi Catering was founded in 2014 by Mireille Duval. The name means the ties made at a shared table: the quiet fact that a meal cooked for a particular room, on a particular day, holds people in the same place for a while. We are a catering kitchen at 14 Wharf Lane, Harbourside. We cook for offices and for family celebrations, and for banquets in halls you hire.

We travel within 40 kilometres. The work runs from a first tasting to the night of service, or, for an office, from a 48-hour order to a table cleared the same afternoon. Mireille is founder and head chef. The company is the six people named on the Kitchen and Team page, not a larger claim.

Meet the kitchen

A kitchen that sets the room first

The moment we cook toward is the one just before the guests arrive. Linen is down, glasses are in rows, and a platter is being set at the near end of a long table. The food is finished in the kitchen at Wharf Lane, then loaded and laid so the room looks complete. That is as true of a meeting-room lunch box as it is of a seated banquet.

We would rather you walk into a table that is already itself than watch a service being improvised. The crew is in three hours before an evening event for that reason. Office drops are planned by Priya Raman so the boxes are on the table at the time you named, not stacked in a corridor waiting for someone to find napkins.

What we hold to

We hold to the numbers we publish. Menus are the seven prices on the Menus page, in US dollars, with the minimums written beside them. Lead time is three weeks for events and 48 hours for office lunches. The deposit is 30 percent. Final numbers are five days before an event. Tastings are $60 for two and credited on the booking.

Staff are $38 an hour. We do the stage we have agreed, and we do not borrow standing from other companies' names. If a date cannot be cooked properly inside those rules, we say so in the reply, which comes within one working day.

The table is yours

The second thing we hold to is that the room is yours. We are guests in a hall, an office or a house. Partner rooms we know, such as the Lantern Rooms, Cedar Assembly Hall and the Long Room at Quay House, are booked by you. A glasshouse, a rowing club or a studio is the same: your contract, our food. We serve the alcohol you buy; we do not sell it.

We clear the things we carried in. The third thing is the shared table itself. A 60th, an engagement dinner and a quarterly all-hands are different shapes, and they are the same job: a counted number of people, a menu tasted or a lunch ordered, and a crew that leaves the table ready. Enishi is that tie, made again each time the table is set.

pages.title: Kitchen & Team
pages.content:
Kitchen & Team

Six people, one kitchen at 14 Wharf Lane. The work is finished before the guests arrive.

Meet the crew

Kitchen 14 Wharf Lane, Harbourside

Founded 2014

Crew in the room 3 hours early

Start an enquiry

Six people, one kitchen

The kitchen is at 14 Wharf Lane, Harbourside. Six people run Enishi Catering. Mireille Duval founded the company in 2014 and is head chef. Tomasz Wren is sous chef. Ayo Okafor is pastry. Lena Hartmann is event manager. Rafael Costa is service lead. Priya Raman is office catering coordinator. On an event day the same group moves from prep at 06:00 to loading at 14:00, setting at 17:00 and service at 19:00.

Office lunches follow a shorter version of that path, with 48 hours' notice. Evening events still need three weeks, a 30 percent deposit and final numbers five days before. The crew is in the room three hours before guests.

Mireille Duval

Founder & head chef

Mireille Duval is founder and head chef. She opened Enishi Catering in 2014 at 14 Wharf Lane. She writes the menus, leads the Thursday and Friday tastings between 14:00 and 17:00, and decides, with the client, what will actually be served. The $60 tasting for two is her table: six small plates, a notebook, and a menu that can still change. She is in the kitchen for the 06:00 prep on service days and remains responsible for the food that leaves in the van. The name she gave the company is a statement of method. The ties are made at the table, so the cooking is planned for that room and that count, from 12 guests up to 180, and then set before anyone arrives.

Tomasz Wren

Sous chef

Tomasz Wren is sous chef. He runs the savoury prep that starts at 06:00: stocks, vegetables, the components of the breakfast table, the lunch boxes and the banquet mains. On a load day he checks the trays before they go into the van at 14:00. During an evening he stays with the food, not the speeches. Office weeks are his as well as Priya's: a minimum of 12 breakfasts at $14 or lunch boxes at $18 has to be cooked and packed on the 48-hour clock, with dietary plates separated exactly as ordered. He works to the final guest count and does not stretch a menu past what was confirmed. If the banquet is three courses at $72, his pass is the middle of the meal.

Ayo Okafor

Pastry

Ayo Okafor is the pastry chef. Cakes for the table, the last course of a seated banquet, and the sweeter of the eight canapé pieces are his. He starts with the morning prep and finishes plates that can travel, because most of what Enishi serves is eaten somewhere other than Wharf Lane. For a birthday he leaves space in his plan for a cake the family is bringing, and he bakes only what was agreed at tasting or on the order. His work sits inside the published prices: there is no separate pastry fee. A family buffet at $46, a seated menu at $72 and a canapé reception at $34 already include the sweet course or pieces described in that menu. He is part of the crew, not a department you hire apart from the event.

Lena Hartmann

Event manager

Lena Hartmann is the event manager. After the enquiry is answered, within one working day, she keeps the date, the 30 percent deposit and the paper trail. Two weeks before an event she turns the tasting notes into a menu and a floor plan the client can mark. Five days before, she receives the final numbers and tells the kitchen the figure that will be cooked. She schedules staff hours at $38 and makes sure the crew's three-hour call before guests is on the run sheet. She is the person who asks what the hall allows, where the van may stand, and when the room must be quiet. Celebrations, banquets and the rare office party that has grown into an evening all sit with her until the night is handed to Rafael.

Rafael Costa

Service lead

Rafael Costa is the service lead. He runs the floor from the moment the crew arrives, three hours before guests, until service ends, no later than 23:30. He sets the standard the hero of this company is built on: napkins, glassware and platters in place before the room fills. At 17:00 on a typical service day he is already dressing the table so that 19:00 is service, not set-up. He briefs the staff who are billed at $38 an hour, places the dietary plates Lena has marked, and serves the client's wine and other drinks without our selling them. A seated plan, a buffet line and a walking canapé service are three different floors. He has led each, including the long tables and the standing receptions.

Priya Raman

Office catering coordinator

Priya Raman coordinates office catering. She is the contact for the working breakfast at $14 and the lunch box set at $18, both with a minimum of 12 and 48 hours' notice, and for afternoon canapés when an office wants the $34 reception, minimum 20. She checks that the address is within 40 kilometres of 14 Wharf Lane, that the delivery time matches a real meeting, and that dietary notes are on the boxes. She works Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 18:00, on +1 555 0142 and hello@enishi-catering.example. When an office lunch grows into a full event, she passes the date to Lena and the three-week engagement begins. Until then she keeps the order short: headcount, time, address, notes, and a collection plan for the crates.

A service day

— PREP, LOAD, SET, SERVE —

STEP 01

Prep

06:00

Mireille, Tomasz and Ayo at the steel benches, trays filling.

STEP 02

Load

14:00

Crates and covered trays go into a plain white van.

STEP 03

Set

17:00

The crew sets linen, glass and the first platters.

STEP 04

Service

19:00

Guests arrive and the kitchen’s work is already in the room.

A service day has four marks. At 06:00 the kitchen is in prep: Mireille, Tomasz and Ayo, trays on steel benches, the menu already fixed by the final numbers. At 14:00 the van is loaded with crates and covered trays. At 17:00 the crew is in the hall setting linen, glass and the first platters; this is inside the three hours before a 19:00 start. At 19:00 service begins. Rafael runs the floor, Lena watches the plan, and the kitchen's work is already in the room.

Not every job uses all four marks. An office lunch may leave in the late morning and never see 19:00. A Sunday family buffet can shift the clock, because events run any day, while the kitchen's office hours for planning stay Tuesday to Saturday. The sequence is the same: prep, load, set, serve.

pages.title: Stories
pages.content:
Stories

Three engagements: a birthday in a rowing club, an engagement dinner in a glasshouse, and an all-hands lunch in a studio.

ROWING CLUB A 60TH BIRTHDAY

Rowing club

The brief was a 60th birthday in a timber rowing-club hall, oars along the wall, no stage and no hotel kitchen. Eighty-four guests, family celebration buffet, $46 a guest. The family had booked the hall. Enishi took the food and the service. We started three weeks out. Two of the family came to 14 Wharf Lane on a Thursday afternoon, paid the $60 tasting, and marked the platters they wanted repeated for eighty-four. That tasting was credited on the booking. The 30 percent deposit held the date. Two weeks before, Lena Hartmann drew a floor plan around the oars, the doors and a long board. Five days before, the family sent the final count: 84, including three plates set aside for dietary needs they had already described.

The crew was in three hours before the first guest. Rafael Costa's team laid linen, set glassware and placed the buffet so the cake stand had a clear end of the table. Staff hours were $38. We did not sell the drinks; the family's bottles were poured beside the buffet. Service wound down well before 23:30, which is as late as we run. We cleared our trays and left the hall to the club. The photograph we kept is the room in the middle of the afternoon, platters open, hands passing a bowl, faces only partly in frame.

Guests84

MenuBuffet · $46

Staff$38 per hour

GLASSHOUSE AN ENGAGEMENT DINNER

Glasshouse

Thirty-six guests, a rented glasshouse, a seated banquet. The couple wanted one long table and three courses, not a room full of rounds. The menu was $72 a guest, minimum 30, so the count of 36 sat just above the floor. They enquired on a Tuesday. We replied the same working day. The tasting was about three weeks before the dinner, $60 for two, credited when they confirmed. Mireille Duval sat with them over six small plates and rewrote the middle course around a dish they had asked to quieten. Two weeks before, the floor plan was a single line: door, table, a place for speeches at the far end, glassware spaced for a narrow aisle. The glasshouse was not one of our regular halls.

It was theirs for the night, within 40 kilometres of Harbourside. Final numbers came five days before and did not change. On the day, prep began at the kitchen in the morning, the van loaded in the afternoon, and the crew was inside three hours before the guests. By the time the couple arrived the table was already set. Rafael led service. Ayo plated the last course. We served the wine the couple had brought; there was nothing from us on a drinks bill. The evening ended before 23:30. What stayed with the kitchen was the length of that one table under the glass, set before anyone sat down.

Guests36

MenuSeated · $72

Staff$38 per hour

STUDIO AN ALL-HANDS LUNCH

Studio

A quarterly all-hands for an architecture studio: 140 guests, lunch boxes plus a short buffet, in a bright studio they already occupied. One hundred and forty is inside our ceiling of 180 and far above the office minimum of 12. The boxes were the office lunch box set at $18. The shared platters followed the family buffet way of laying food, priced with the studio as an agreed addition to the lunch so people could gather after they had eaten, rather than as a second unknown rate. Priya Raman ran the order. Because of the size, the studio gave us more than the usual 48 hours; the date was planned on the event clock, with a 30 percent deposit and a final count five days before.

Dietary notes were printed on box lids for the people Priya had listed, and the buffet platters stayed free of those conflicts. The van arrived in the late morning. We laid boxes and bread on the long studio tables, then the platters at one end. No evening crew, no 19:00 service: this was a working day, and the team was back at desks. We collected crates before the end of the afternoon. The studio did not need staff for a reception, so the $38 hour barely appeared; two people delivered, set and cleared. It remains our clearest office story: a large count, a simple menu, a room that was already theirs.

Guests140

MenuLunch boxes + buffet

Deposit30 %

pages.title: FAQ
pages.content:
FAQ

Ten questions we are asked most, answered with the same numbers as everywhere else.

Can you cook for particular dietary needs?

Yes, when we know in time to buy and prep. Tell us at the enquiry or the tasting, and repeat the note with the final guest numbers five days before an event, or with the office order that needs 48 hours. The plate is the menu you chose, adjusted, not a separate price. Priya Raman marks office boxes. Lena Hartmann puts evening notes on the floor plan so Rafael Costa's service does not guess.

We do not publish a closed list of diets, and we do not claim a need can be met if we hear about it on the night. If a request cannot be cooked inside the menu you booked, we will say so when we reply, within one working day.

How much notice do you need?

Events need three weeks. That stretch covers the enquiry, the tasting about three weeks before, the menu and floor plan two weeks before, and the final numbers five days before. Office lunches need 48 hours, with a minimum of 12 guests for the working breakfast at $14 or the lunch box set at $18. A canapé reception, including an office afternoon, needs a minimum of 20 and, if it is part of an evening, the three-week lead.

We reply to a new enquiry within one working day. Planning hours are Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 18:00. Events themselves may fall on any day and run until 23:30. The kitchen is at 14 Wharf Lane, Harbourside.

How does the deposit work?

The deposit is 30 percent and it confirms the date. It applies to events on the three-week path. The tasting fee is separate: $60 for two, credited on the booking, so it comes off what you owe when the event is confirmed. The rest of the bill follows the final guest count, due five days before, and the staff hours at $38 per staff hour.

Office breakfasts and lunch boxes ordered on the 48-hour clock are confirmed by Priya Raman without the ceremony of a full engagement, unless the job has grown large enough to plan as an event, as the studio lunch for 140 did. We state the 30 percent figure in the reply. We do not add a second deposit rate.

What if we have to cancel or change the count?

Write to us as soon as the date moves. We do not publish a ladder of cancellation fees beyond the figures already on this site. The 30 percent deposit is what held the date, and the kitchen buys to the final numbers you send five days before. A change before that lock can still be reflected in the count we cook. A change after it meets food that is already committed to the number you gave.

Office orders sit on a 48-hour clock, so a change has to reach Priya Raman before prep, not the morning of delivery. Contact hello@enishi-catering.example or +1 555 0142, Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 18:00. We will tell you, in that reply, what can still move.

What equipment do you bring?

We bring the food, the service we have agreed, and what we need to dress the table we are responsible for: linen and glassware for the places we set, platters and trays, and the crates they travel in. We do not bring the hall. Tables, chairs and the room are yours, or the venue's. Tell us in the enquiry what is already there so the floor plan, drawn two weeks before, matches the furniture rather than imagining it.

The crew arrives three hours before evening guests to do the setting. If you need staff to stay, they are $38 an hour. We load in a plain van and we take our crates away at the end.

What happens to leftover food and waste?

We cook to the final guest count: the number you send five days before an event, or the number on the office order placed with 48 hours' notice. Portioning starts there, so we are not guessing on the morning. After service we clear what we brought, including trays, crates and the remains of our service. The room, and any drinks you supplied, stay with you.

We do not leave a claim about composting rates or certificates, because we do not publish one. If the hall has its own rule for waste, tell Lena Hartmann when the floor plan is drawn and the crew will follow that rule alongside our own clear-up. The aim is a table that was full at the start and a room that is not full of our equipment at the end.

Where do you travel?

We cook at 14 Wharf Lane, Harbourside, and we serve within 40 kilometres of that kitchen. The area includes offices, homes and hired halls. Rooms we already know as a caterer, not as a venue owner, include the Lantern Rooms in Harbourside, Cedar Assembly Hall and the Long Room at Quay House.

You book the room. We book the food. If the address is outside 40 kilometres we will say so in the reply, within one working day, and we will not stretch the van past the area. Guest counts for any address inside the area still have to sit between the menu minimum and 180.

Do you provide alcohol?

We do not sell alcohol. We serve the client's. If wine or another drink is part of the evening, you buy it and we pour it as part of service. Staff time for that pouring is the same $38 per staff hour as the rest of the floor. It is not a corkage price and not a bar tariff, because there is no bar on our list.

Tell Rafael Costa's team, through the enquiry, what you are bringing and when it will be at the venue, so the three-hour set-up includes the glasses. Office lunches rarely need this. A 60th or an engagement dinner often does. The drinks never appear as a line invented by the kitchen.

How many guests can you take?

The company range is 12 to 180 guests. Each menu also has its own minimum. Working breakfast and office lunch boxes: 12. Canapé reception, eight pieces: 20. Family celebration buffet: 20. Seated banquet, three courses: 30. A party below the menu minimum needs a different card or a different count.

A party above 180 is outside what this kitchen schedules. The rowing-club birthday was 84 on the buffet. The glasshouse engagement was 36 seated. The studio all-hands was 140, lunch boxes plus a buffet. Those three sit inside the same range. Final numbers, five days before, are the count we cook.

How does a tasting work, and what does it cost?

A tasting is for two people and costs $60. The $60 is credited on the booking. It is held about three weeks before the event, on Thursday or Friday, 14:00 to 17:00, at 14 Wharf Lane, Harbourside. You taste six small plates with the chef and leave with notes that become the menu. Two weeks before the date, that menu and the floor plan are confirmed.

Office breakfasts and standard lunch boxes do not require a tasting; you may still book one if an office order is becoming a larger event. Slots are limited to those two afternoons. Write to hello@enishi-catering.example or call +1 555 0142 in office hours, Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 18:00, and we will reply within one working day.

Still unsure?

Write to us with the date, the place and a first count. We reply within one working day.

Finding the kitchen

14 Wharf Lane, Harbourside is the kitchen address. There is no embedded map on this page. Look up 14 Wharf Lane, Harbourside in whatever map you use, and you will be looking for the catering kitchen, not a dining room with seats for the public. Tastings are the main reason to come to the door, and only at a booked slot on Thursday or Friday, 14:00 to 17:00. Office lunches and banquets are cooked here and eaten somewhere else within 40 kilometres.

If you are unsure whether a venue is inside that circle, send the address in the enquiry. We would rather answer within one working day than have a van committed past the area. Parking and load-in for the kitchen itself are arranged when your visit is a tasting, not a collection of a finished banquet.

Tasting slots

Tastings run Thursday and Friday, 14:00 to 17:00, for two people, at $60, credited on the booking. They sit about three weeks before an event, which is stage 02 of an engagement. Ask for a slot in the form by naming the event date and which afternoon you can travel to Harbourside. We confirm the time in the reply, inside one working day, during Tuesday to Saturday office hours.

Come with a sense of the room and the count. Leave with a menu the floor plan can be drawn from, two weeks before the date. If you need a plate adjusted for a dietary reason, this is the right hour to taste the alternative, while there is still time to buy for the final numbers.

posts.title: Set before they arrive: a service day at Wharf Lane
posts.excerpt: From the 06:00 prep at 14 Wharf Lane to a table that is already finished three hours before the guests, this is how one Enishi engagement actually runs.
posts.content:
The useful hour at Enishi Catering is not the first minute of dinner. It is the stretch before anyone arrives, when the table is already a finished scene. Mireille Duval founded the company in 2014 around that idea. The name means the ties made at a shared table. The method is more ordinary than the phrase: a counted guest list, a menu that was tasted, a crew that enters the room three hours early, and a van that leaves again with its own crates.

A service day at the kitchen on 14 Wharf Lane, Harbourside, is marked in four times. At 06:00 the prep begins. Tomasz Wren has the savoury benches. Ayo Okafor has pastry. Mireille keeps the menu that was agreed two weeks before and the guest count that arrived five days before. Nothing in that kitchen is still a draft. The tasting, if there was one, happened about three weeks earlier: two people, six small plates, $60, credited on the booking, on a Thursday or a Friday between 14:00 and 17:00.

At 14:00 the van is loaded. Covered trays, crates, linen and the glassware for the places Enishi will set go into a plain white van. The address on the run sheet sits inside 40 kilometres. Beyond that circle the job is declined in the enquiry reply, which goes out within one working day. Lena Hartmann has already checked the hall's load-in notes. The room itself is never ours. A client may be in the Lantern Rooms, in Cedar Assembly Hall, in the Long Room at Quay House, or in a glasshouse, a rowing club or a studio they booked themselves.

At 17:00, for an evening that will start at 19:00, the crew is setting. Rafael Costa leads the floor. Napkins, glasses and the first platter are placed while the chairs are still pushed in and the light is still coming from the windows. This is the whole of the early arrival: three hours in which service is setting, not apologising. Staff hours are $38. Those hours include this quiet part, not only the plated hour.

At 19:00 the guests are due, and service begins. A seated banquet is three courses at $72 a guest, minimum 30. A family celebration buffet is $46, minimum 20. A canapé reception is eight pieces at $34, minimum 20. The company will cook for as few as 12 and as many as 180, but the menu minimum still applies. We do not sell alcohol. If there is wine, it is the client's, and Rafael's team pours it. Service ends by 23:30 even when the hall would stay open later. Then the crates go back to the van.

Not every day uses the 19:00 mark. Office catering runs on a shorter clock: 48 hours' notice, minimum 12, coordinated by Priya Raman. A working breakfast table is $14 a guest. An office lunch box set is $18. The food is still cooked on Wharf Lane and laid as a finished spread on someone else's meeting table. When an office party grows up, as a quarterly all-hands for 140 once did, it leaves the 48-hour path, takes a 30 percent deposit, and locks its count five days out.

The deposit is the other ordinary fact. Thirty percent confirms an event date. Final numbers five days before confirm what the kitchen buys. Between those two points the floor plan is drawn, two weeks out, from the tasting notes and from what the client tells us about the room. We do not bring tables and chairs. We bring the food and the setting for the table we are responsible for, and we clear it afterwards.

Three evenings are enough to see the range, because the range is not very wide. Eighty-four guests stood and sat down to a buffet in a timber rowing-club hall for a 60th birthday. Thirty-six guests sat at one long table in a rented glasshouse for an engagement dinner, three courses, the $60 tasting already credited. One hundred and forty people in an architecture studio took lunch boxes and a short buffet and went back to their desks. Same kitchen, same published prices, different rooms.

Enquiries come in by the form, by +1 555 0142, or by hello@enishi-catering.example. Office hours for that correspondence are Tuesday to Saturday, 09:00 to 18:00. The reply fits inside one working day. If the date can be cooked inside the lead time, the minimum and the 40-kilometre circle, the next sentence is a tasting slot or a confirmation of the deposit. If it cannot, the reply says that too.

What the guest sees, if the day has gone to plan, is none of this schedule. They see a long table in a hired room, linen already down, a platter at the near end, and a crew that looks as if it has been there longer than three hours. That picture is the whole advertisement we are willing to make. The ties at the table are real only when the food is ready before the first chair moves.
